front: Merge Sort: worst, best, and average case complexity?
back: Θ(n log n) in all three cases — merging always costs Θ(n) regardless of input order.

front: When does Quicksort hit its Θ(n²) worst case?
back: When the pivot is always the minimum or maximum of the current subarray (e.g. sorted input with first-element pivot), causing maximally unbalanced partitions.

front: Why is Quicksort often faster than Merge Sort in practice despite the same average complexity?
back: Quicksort sorts in place (no temp array copying) and has smaller constant factors.

front: How does randomizing the pivot choice help Quicksort?
back: It avoids the worst case on already-sorted or adversarially-ordered input, making Θ(n log n) the expected running time regardless of input order.

front: What is the lower bound for any comparison-based sorting algorithm, and why?
back: Ω(n log n) — from a decision-tree argument: there are n! orderings, each comparison distinguishes 2 outcomes, so tree depth ≥ log₂(n!) = Θ(n log n).

front: Where does Merge Sort do its 'real work': divide or combine? And Quicksort?
back: Merge Sort: trivial divide, real work in combine (the merge step). Quicksort: real work in divide (the partition step), trivial combine (nothing to do).
